title: [OC] How often a live Bitcoin forecast's 90% range caught the price, day by day, at 1h, 4h and 24h ahead
author: Immediate_Finish6422

comments.author: Immediate_Finish6422
comments.body:
Source: my own live forecasts, scored automatically against Binance BTC/USDT prices (5-minute bars), 28 Oct to 5 Nov 2026. The raw daily numbers are public as JSON at [https://btcforecaster.com/api/live-stats](https://btcforecaster.com/api/live-stats) (the "daily" entries for the v2 model).

Tool: SVG chart generated with a script, rendered to PNG with Playwright.

How to read it: every 5 minutes the model gives a range the price should land in 1, 4 or 24 hours later, 90% of the time. Each bar is the share of that day's forecasts (about 288) that landed inside. A well-calibrated range should sit near the dashed 90% line, so 100% isn't "perfect", it means the ranges were wider than needed.

What stands out to me: the 1-hour forecast stays close to target almost every day, but the 24-hour one swings from 100% to 21%. Both bad stretches came right after calm days. The model learns from recent movement, so after a quiet spell it narrows its ranges, and the next big move breaks through.

Happy to answer questions about the method or share the raw numbers.
